nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The primary response variable is PBSI-SW (Person-Based Similarity Index for Sulcal Width), a multivariate summary measure that quantifies an individual's morphometric similarity across 11 bilateral sulcal regions compared to healthy controls. Sulcal width (SW) is defined as the distance between each gyral bank averaged over all points along the median sulcal surface. The PBSI-SW was calculated using Spearman's rank correlation coefficients between SW profiles.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: We calculated the PBSI for sulcal width (PBSI-SW) in patients with schizophrenia and healthy control subjects; The PBSI-SW calculation was based on 16. At each time point and for each individual, we computed a PBSI-SW value using a 3-step procedure; Sulcal width is defined as the distance between each gyral bank averaged over all points along the median sulcal surface.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: GAMMs modeled age and diagnosis with an age × diagnosis interaction, controlling for scanner and total brain volume with a random effect of the individual.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs) were used. GAMM models were implemented to examine age, diagnosis (ie, patient vs control), and an age × diagnosis interaction while controlling for scanner, total brain volume, and the random effect of the individual.
